U11 / Atom.sit: You are a forward at the left face-off dot in the offensive zone. Your teammate passes the puck from behind the net and it is sliding toward you. What should you do while the puck is still on its way?
opts: Step forward to meet the puck early and use your body to shield possession
Keep your eyes fixed on the puck so it lands cleanly on your stick blade
Shout to an open teammate to let them know where you plan to pass next
Peek over both shoulders so you know your next move when the puck arrives
U11 / Atom.explain: The puck-travel window is your best chance to look around before you receive it. A quick shoulder check gives you a picture of the ice, so the moment the puck touches your stick you already know where defenders are and who is open.

U11 / Atom.sit: You carry the puck on a 2-on-1. The lone defender slides over and takes away the pass to your teammate. What is the highest-value decision?
opts: Shoot — the defender committed to the pass, so the lane to the net is open
Force the pass through the defender anyway
Turn back to your own end and regroup
Dump the puck into the corner
U11 / Atom.explain: When the defender commits to taking away the pass, they have given you the shooting lane. Reading what the defender takes away tells you what is open.

U11 / Atom.sit: 3-on-2 rush. You are the middle driver without the puck. The puck carrier is wide on the right. What should you do?
opts: Drive hard to the net for a pass or rebound
Curl back toward the blue line
Stop at the top of the circles and wait
Skate to the same side as the puck carrier
U11 / Atom.explain: On a 3-on-2 the middle lane drives the net — it forces the defence to honour you and opens a pass or a rebound. Spreading the attack stretches two defenders across three lanes.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are a white player skating up the right side. A pass from your teammate is on its way, and a black defender has been trailing you since the last faceoff. You have not looked back since the play started. What is the most important thing to do before the puck reaches you?
opts: Call to your teammate to hold the puck longer
Scan behind you to find where the pressure is
Speed up to create separation before it arrives
Focus on the puck so you do not miss the catch
U11 / Atom.explain: If you catch the puck without knowing where the black defender is, you will have no time to make a good play once it arrives. A quick look back first tells you exactly what options you have.

U11 / Atom.sit: The white team's winger grabs a loose puck at center ice. You look back and see both of your black team's defenders are still deep in the offensive zone. What does this pattern tell you is developing?
opts: A dangerous mismatch is forming toward your net
Your black teammates will catch up before trouble starts
Your goalie should expect just a single attacker
They will likely slow down and dump it deep
U11 / Atom.explain: When both your defenders are still in the other end, the white team has more attackers heading toward your net than you have back. Reading that mismatch before it forms is what lets you turn and backcheck at full speed.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are the center at center ice, carrying the puck. The white jersey defender at the far blue line is standing still, flat-footed. Open ice stretches ahead of you. What is the best play?
opts: Attack quickly before the gap to the zone closes
Hold up and draw the defender out before attacking
Slow down and wait for your wingers to arrive
Reverse and pass back to reset with your defensemen
U11 / Atom.explain: The defender is flat-footed, which means space is open right now. If you pause or hold up, the defender has time to recover their stance and the lane to the zone disappears.

U11 / Atom.sit: In an offensive-zone corner battle, you push past a white defender and knock the puck free. It slides to the open ice in front of the net. The defender is behind you, still finding their balance. What should you do next?
opts: Skate a wide arc around the outside before cutting toward the loose puck
Rush toward the loose puck and put a shot on net right away
Slow your pace and look around before deciding where to go next
Hold your spot near the boards in case the play comes back to you
U11 / Atom.explain: When the puck is free and the defender is still finding their balance, that is your window to act. Bursting straight to the puck and shooting right away finishes the job before they can recover. Slowing down, going wide, or staying near the boards all hand the defender the extra second they need to get back in position.

U11 / Atom.sit: You have the puck at center ice, carrying toward the offensive zone. A white defender steps up from the right side. To your left, a black teammate has moved into open space behind the defender. What gives you the best chance to use your teammate's position?
opts: Driving hard to the net before the defender reacts
Watching the defender's feet to time your move around them
Scanning the ice while keeping the puck under control
Protecting the puck low and tight as the defender closes in
U11 / Atom.explain: Scanning the ice while you carry lets you see your black teammate in open space before the white defender cuts off your options. Locking your focus on the puck or the defender alone means you miss the pass that gives your team the better chance.

U11 / Atom.sit: You carry the puck into the offensive zone on a 2-on-1. The lone defender charges toward you to take away your angle. Your teammate is streaking to the far side of the net with no defender near them. What is the best play?
opts: Pass to your teammate cutting hard to the far post
Snap a shot at the near side of the net
Deke around the defender and drive to the net yourself
Slow down near the blue line and regroup with help
U11 / Atom.explain: When the defender charges toward you, they stop covering your teammate's side of the net, and a pass creates a much cleaner look at the goal. Shooting at a closing defender when your teammate is completely free means choosing the harder chance over the better one.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are a center with the puck skating into the neutral zone. The middle lane ahead is clear all the way to the offensive blue line. The nearest defender is 12 feet to your side, angled toward the boards and out of your path. Both wingers have opposing players tight on them. What is your best read?
opts: Skate forward and carry the puck through the middle
Chip the puck ahead and race the defender to it
Pass the puck back to your trailing defenseman
Send a quick cross-ice pass to one of your wingers
U11 / Atom.explain: The lane ahead is clear and the defender is off to the side with no angle on you, so you have time and space, the two ingredients that tell you to keep the puck and use that room. Chipping gives up possession when nothing is actually forcing you off the puck, and both wingers are guarded, so carrying forward through that open lane is the right read.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are defending in your own zone. Your defensive partner is tracking the white puck carrier near the left boards. The puck carrier pivots to face the net, and at that same moment a second white attacker cuts toward the open ice near the crease. What should you do right now?
opts: Fall back toward your own goal line to protect the net
Step up and cut off the second attacker before they reach the net
Skate to the boards to help your partner pressure the puck carrier
Hold your position mid-ice and wait for the play to develop
U11 / Atom.explain: The puck carrier pivoting to face the net while the second attacker moves toward the crease tells you a pass to the front is forming right now, and since your partner already has the puck carrier covered, stepping up to cut off that attacker is the read. Waiting lets that attacker get set up before the puck even moves, and skating to the boards to help your partner leaves the front of the net completely open.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are a forward in the neutral zone. Your defenseman sends a crisp pass that will reach your stick in about two seconds. You are already in a smooth skating stride and balanced. A defender is skating toward you but has not closed in yet. What is the best thing to do in those two seconds?
opts: Watch the puck to your stick before checking for an open teammate.
Look around now so your next move is ready when you receive.
Ease up so your feet are planted for a cleaner first touch.
Turn your upper body to shield the puck from the closing defender.
U11 / Atom.explain: Because you have two seconds and the defender has not closed in yet, a quick look around lets you spot open teammates so your next play is ready the moment the puck arrives. Watching the puck all the way to your stick or turning to shield early are both tempting, but they use up the only window you had to look, leaving you to decide under pressure instead of acting on a read you already made.

U11 / Atom.sit: You carry the puck at the left dot. Your teammate breaks from the boards toward the slot, one step in front of the defender chasing behind them. The area in front of the net is uncovered. What is the best play?
opts: Pass the puck into the space your teammate is entering
Hold the puck and wait for a clearer lane
Pass the puck to where your teammate is right now
Shoot the puck on net from the left dot
U11 / Atom.explain: Your teammate already has a step on the defender, so the window to act is now and the puck needs to arrive where they will be, not where they started. Passing to their current spot lets the defender close in as your teammate skates right past the puck. Shooting from the dot gives up the uncovered area in front of the net that your teammate has already worked to create.

U11 / Atom.sit: You and an opponent are battling for the puck along the boards in your own zone. The puck squirts free and slides a few feet into open ice. You are the closest player, but the opponent is right behind you. What is the best thing to do right now?
opts: Skate back toward your net and set up in a good defensive position
Slow down and tie up the opponent's stick before going to the puck
Wait to see where the puck slides before committing to go get it
Sprint to the puck right away and use your body to shield it
U11 / Atom.explain: When you are the closest player to a loose puck, going to it right away and shielding it with your body is how you win the battle. Stopping to tie up the opponent or waiting to see where it slides both give them time to close the gap and take possession.

interaction.prompt: You hold the puck at the blue line. The play is developing — nobody is rushing you yet. Tap the teammate who has the most time and space right now.

feedback.right: The LW on the weak-side wall has a huge gap — no defender within range. That open pocket is exactly where the puck should go.
feedback.wrong: Check the defenders: one is tight on the C in the slot, and the other is glued to the RW down low. The LW on the far side has no one near them — that's the player with time and space.

U11 / Atom.tip: Before you pass, scan for the jersey with the biggest gap to the nearest opponent. The player with the most space has the most time — they are your best option.
U11 / Atom.why: Both defenders collapsed toward the middle and strong side, leaving the weak-side LW completely unchecked with room to receive and make a quality play.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are the first forward entering the offensive zone with the puck. The defenseman is backing up quickly. What should you scan for first?
opts: Whether a teammate behind you is calling for a drop pass
The space between you and the backing up defenseman to see if you have room to skate
Whether a late teammate is joining the rush for a pass after you cross the blue line
Whether the goalie is set before you reach the top of the circle
U11 / Atom.explain: The first read is the defender's gap. If the defenseman is backing up and leaving room, a U11 puck carrier can keep skating and attack the space. If the gap closes, then it is time to delay, pass, or chip to support.

U11 / Atom.sit: When skating back to retrieve a puck in your defensive corner, you should wait until the puck is on your stick before looking around so you do not lose control of it.
U11 / Atom.tip: Check your shoulder before the puck arrives.
U11 / Atom.why: A quick look before the touch helps you know where the forechecker is and where your support is. Then your first touch can protect the puck or move it to an open teammate.

U11 / Atom.sit: A winger is waiting on the boards for a breakout pass. They stare directly at the puck the entire time it slides toward them, catch it, and immediately get checked.
U11 / Atom.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They stayed too flat-footed instead of taking a step toward open ice
They failed to shoulder check into the middle of the ice to see the incoming pressure
They should have chipped the puck past the defender before trying to catch it
They caught the pass on the boards instead of moving closer to the hash marks
U11 / Atom.explain: The biggest mistake is not checking inside before the puck arrives. At U11, a winger on the boards should take a quick look so they know whether they have time to turn up ice, need to protect the puck, or should make a quick touch pass.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are the center supporting your defenseman low in the zone. You see your winger is open on the far boards and you have a clear passing lane, but a forechecker is skating hard at you.
opts: Turn back below the goal line and try to beat the forechecker one-on-one
One-touch pass the puck quickly to the open winger on the far boards before the pressure hits
Hold the puck for an extra second to see if your defenseman gets open again
Rim the puck hard around the boards even though your winger is already open
U11 / Atom.explain: Because you already scanned and found the open winger, the smart play is to move the puck before the forechecker arrives. A quick pass away from pressure is safer than holding it in a low-danger area of your own zone.
U11 / Atom.tip: Use your scan early so your pass can be quick.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are playing defense and catch a pass at the offensive blue line. Before you decide to shoot, what is the most important thing to scan the scoring area for?
opts: Whether a forward is calling for the puck near the corner
If there is a clear lane to the net and if you have a teammate screening the goalie
Whether your defense partner is open for a safety pass across the blue line
If the goalie is leaning before you have checked for blockers in the lane
U11 / Atom.explain: A point shot is useful when it can get through. At U11, the defender should look for a clear lane and friendly traffic first, because shooting into shin pads often turns into a rush the other way.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are the first player back for a puck retrieval. Put these actions in the correct order to make a smart play.
items: Collect the puck on your stick with your body ready to protect it
Make a crisp pass to your supporting teammate
Take a quick shoulder check to locate the forechecker
Use your skating edges to create separation from the pressure
U11 / Atom.explain: The first look gives you a plan before you touch the puck. After that, collect it, create a little space from pressure, and move it to support with control.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are away from the puck in the offensive zone while your teammate is battling in the corner. How should you use your eyes?
opts: Watch only the puck battle so you can react the moment it comes free
Keep your head on a swivel to find an open pocket of space away from defenders
Drift closer to the corner so your teammate has a shorter pass
Look back toward the blue line first in case your defenseman wants the puck
U11 / Atom.explain: Scanning away from the puck helps you find soft spots in coverage. If your teammate wins the battle, you are already available instead of skating into the same crowded area.

U11 / Atom.sit: You are regrouping in the neutral zone. You look up and see the opposing defensemen are standing still at their blue line with loose gaps. What is your next move?
opts: Chip the puck softly into the corner even though you have room to skate
Pass the puck backward right away to restart the regroup
Attack the space with speed to force them to pivot or back up
Slow down at the blue line and wait for them to choose a side
U11 / Atom.explain: Still defenders with loose gaps are vulnerable to speed. If you scan their feet and see they are flat, attack before they can match your pace.
U11 / Atom.tip: Flat feet are a cue to attack with speed.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck and your teammate is skating up the middle with no one near them. A defender is reaching for you. What is the best play?
opts: Pass it to your open teammate in the middle
Hold onto it and try to skate around the defender
Shoot it all the way down the ice
Stop and wait for help
U9 / Novice.explain: An open teammate with speed up the middle is the best option. A good pass beats a stickhandle when a defender is already on you.

U9 / Novice.sit: You carry the puck into the corner of the attacking zone. A white-jersey teammate is standing alone right in front of the net. A black-jersey defender is skating toward you. What is the best play?
opts: Fire a shot at the net from where you stand
Skate back toward center ice with the puck
Send a pass to your teammate for a close-range chance
Wait near the boards until more room opens up
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate is alone in the best scoring spot on the ice. A pass from the corner sets up a much better chance than a low-angle shot from where you are standing.

U9 / Novice.sit: You are a white-jersey player in the neutral zone. You see two black-jersey players racing toward your end, and they are ahead of all your white-jersey teammates. What does this tell you is most likely about to happen?
opts: The black players will be called for offside
Your team will recover before the rush hits
A scoring chance is developing against your team
Your goalie can stop the play without help
U9 / Novice.explain: When two black-jersey players are ahead of all your white-jersey teammates, that is a sign a dangerous rush is heading toward your end. Spotting that pattern early gives your whole team a chance to get back and protect your goalie.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck on the side boards deep in the offensive zone. A teammate is standing right in front of the net with no defender nearby. What is the best play?
opts: Shoot at the goalie from your spot on the boards
Carry the puck toward the net for a closer shot
Hold onto the puck and try to stickhandle through
Pass the puck to the teammate waiting at the net
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate is already set up at the front of the net with nobody around them, which is the best spot to score from. A quick pass gets the puck there right away, giving your team a much better chance than shooting from the tough side-boards angle.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate has the puck near the boards and is about to send you a pass on the wing. You have a second before it arrives. What should you do in that moment?
opts: Keep your eyes on the puck as it comes
Turn your head to check who is near you
Skate toward your teammate to shorten the pass
Call out to show your teammate you are open
U9 / Novice.explain: The moment before the puck arrives is your best chance to see who is nearby. Watching only the puck while it travels is tempting, but once it hits your stick the chance to look is gone, so a quick check now gives you a head start on your next play.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck in the corner near the net. A defender is skating toward you quickly. Your teammate is standing all alone at the front of the net. What is the best play?
opts: Try to skate past the defender with the puck
Pass to your teammate at the front of the net
Skate back up the ice to find more space
Shoot the puck toward the net from the corner
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate at the front of the net is in a great spot to score. From the corner, the net is hard to hit cleanly, but your teammate has a clear look at it.

U9 / Novice.sit: Your teammate is about to pass you the puck in the neutral zone. What is the best thing to do in the moment before the puck arrives?
opts: Skate straight toward the opponent's net to get into position
Wait until the puck arrives to plan your next move
Keep both eyes locked on the puck coming your way
Take a quick look around to spot who is open
U9 / Novice.explain: That moment before the puck arrives is your chance to look around, so you already know where to go the instant you catch it. If you stare at the puck instead, you will have no plan ready when it lands on your stick.

U9 / Novice.sit: You have the puck at the top of the circles in the offensive zone. Your teammate is standing alone near the front of the net, with no defender close by. The goalie is set in the crease watching you. What is the best play?
opts: Take a shot from the top of the circles
Skate the puck back toward center ice
Carry the puck into the near corner
Pass to your teammate near the front of the net
U9 / Novice.explain: Your teammate near the front of the net is open and in a much better scoring spot. The goalie is already set and watching you, so sending the puck to your close, open teammate gives your team a better chance to score than shooting from farther away.

interaction.prompt: Your team has the puck in the zone. Which teammate has the most time and space right now?

feedback.right: Great read! Your teammate near the top boards has lots of room — the nearest defender is back covering the slot, several metres away. They have all the time they need to receive and make the next play.
feedback.wrong: Your teammate along the bottom boards looks available, but a defender is right on their shoulder. The moment that pass arrives they will be under pressure. Your teammate up top has much more space right now.

U9 / Novice.tip: Before every pass, check how many steps separate each teammate from the nearest defender — a bigger gap means more time and space to work with.
U9 / Novice.why: Scanning for separation around teammates is the first building block of every smart pass decision in the offensive zone.

U7 / Initiation.sit: You have the puck and your teammate is skating up the middle with no one near them. A defender is reaching for you. What is the best play?
opts: Pass it to your open teammate in the middle
Hold onto it and try to skate around the defender
Shoot it all the way down the ice
Stop and wait for help
U7 / Initiation.explain: An open teammate with speed up the middle is the best option. A good pass beats a stickhandle when a defender is already on you.

U13 / Peewee.sit: 3-on-2 rush. You are the middle driver without the puck. The puck carrier is wide on the right. What should you do?
opts: Drive hard to the net for a pass or rebound
Curl back toward the blue line
Stop at the top of the circles and wait
Skate to the same side as the puck carrier
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 3-on-2 the middle lane drives the net — it forces the defence to honour you and opens a pass or a rebound. Spreading the attack stretches two defenders across three lanes.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the lone defender on a 2-on-1. The puck carrier is winding up to shoot. What is your job?
opts: Take away the pass and let your goalie have the shot
Slide to block the shot and leave the pass open
Skate at the puck carrier to try a poke check
Back all the way in to the net
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 2-on-1 the defender takes away the pass and trusts the goalie to handle the shot. A shooter the goalie can see is a better outcome than a back-door tap-in.

U13 / Peewee.sit: Your defenseman is about to send you a breakout pass in your own zone. Your eyes have been on the puck since the play started, so you have no idea where the nearest opposing player is. The puck is about two seconds away from reaching you. What is the most important thing to do right now?
opts: Skate into open ice to put distance between yourself and any defender
Let your defenseman know you are ready by calling out to them
Do a quick shoulder check to spot pressure and find open teammates
Keep your eyes on the puck to make sure you receive it cleanly
U13 / Peewee.explain: Before the puck arrives is your last chance to collect information, so a quick shoulder check tells you where pressure is coming from and which teammates are open. If you catch the puck without that read, you will be reacting to what you find instead of already knowing your best option.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are the right wing in the neutral zone. Your black-jersey teammate has the puck and is about to pass it your way. A white-jersey defender is nearby, watching you closely. You just found open space. What is the most important thing to do before the puck arrives?
opts: Signal your teammate to hold the pass for a moment
Keep both eyes on the puck so you don't miss the catch
Position your body toward the boards for puck protection
Take a quick look around to see where the pressure is
U13 / Peewee.explain: A quick look around before the puck reaches you tells you exactly where that white-jersey defender is, so you already have a plan the moment you catch it. Watching the puck, signaling a hold, or pre-positioning your body all leave you blind to that defender's location when the puck lands.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You have the puck on the half-wall in the offensive zone. The goalie is set and ready to stop a shot from where you are standing. Your teammate is open in the high-danger area right in front of the net, with no defender close enough to challenge them. A defender is closing toward you. What is the best play?
opts: Skate across the zone to get a better shooting angle
Carry the puck in toward the net yourself
Send it to your teammate in front right away
Shoot from your current spot on the wall
U13 / Peewee.explain: Your teammate is standing in the high-danger area with no one near them, so a quick pass gives them a clean shot before any defender arrives. A shot from the wall is low-percentage here because the goalie is already in position to cover it.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are bringing the puck up the ice on a rush. You see the first layer of defense stepping up on you. Why is it critical to scan the second layer behind them?
opts: To know if you can chip the puck into space and retrieve it behind the first defender
To see if the far winger is open before you decide whether the chip is safe
To decide if you should slow down and wait for a trailer behind you
So you can immediately turn back and reset the breakout the moment you spot a second defender
U13 / Peewee.explain: Scanning beyond the first defender tells you whether there is usable space behind pressure. If the second layer is too close, a chip can become a turnover. If there is space, an area play can let you keep speed.

U13 / Peewee.sit: When playing weak-side wing in the defensive zone, it is best to stay locked onto the puck so you never lose track of the play.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Scan between the puck and your check.
U13 / Peewee.why: If you stare only at the puck, you can lose the weak-side threat in the slot or at the point. A U13 winger should keep switching their eyes between the puck, open opponents, and their coverage job.

U13 / Peewee.sit: A defenseman receives a D-to-D pass in the neutral zone. They look down to catch it cleanly, hold onto it for three seconds while looking for a pass, and get pressured by the forechecker.
U13 / Peewee.question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They called for the pass while standing still instead of building speed
They failed to scan up the ice before the pass arrived, resulting in slow decision making
They should have reversed the puck back to their partner immediately
They held the puck in the middle lane instead of moving it toward the boards
U13 / Peewee.explain: Pre-scanning lets the defenseman know the next option before the puck arrives. Without that early look, they spend too long processing after the catch and give the forechecker time to close.

U13 / Peewee.sit: Your team is cycling the puck low in the offensive zone. You are the high forward (F3). You scan the slot and see it is open.
opts: Back all the way out toward the red line to protect against a turnover
Slide into the open high slot, show your stick, and stay ready to recover if possession changes
Skate down below the goal line to make it a three-player puck battle
Stay wide near the boards and wait for a rim or rebound
U13 / Peewee.explain: F3 can become a scoring option when quiet ice opens, but they still need defensive awareness. Sliding into the high slot with a target gives the puck carrier an option without abandoning responsibility above the puck.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Find quiet ice without giving up your safety role.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are a winger slashing across the neutral zone to receive a breakout pass. Order the steps for a successful entry.
items: Catch the puck in stride while maintaining your speed
Scan the offensive blue line to locate the defensemen's gap
Use the gap read to decide whether to carry, chip, or pass
Present a clear target with your stick to your passing defenseman
U13 / Peewee.explain: The winger should read the gap before asking for the puck. Catching in stride matters, and the earlier scan helps the player choose the entry before the defense can close.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You are a defenseman defending a 2-on-1 rush. What should your eyes be doing as the play crosses your blue line?
opts: Lock only on the puck carrier and angle hard toward them
Look mostly at the puck so you are ready to block the shot
Quickly shifting focus back and forth between the puck carrier and the dangerous pass option
Watch the puck carrier's skates so you can time a poke check
U13 / Peewee.explain: On a 2-on-1, the defender must manage both threats. Scanning between the puck carrier and the passing option helps you protect the middle, take away the most dangerous pass, and avoid chasing one player too early.

U13 / Peewee.sit: You pick up a loose puck in the high slot of your defensive zone. You feel pressure right on your back, but you have not scanned up the ice yet.
opts: Chip a backhand pass toward the middle and hope a teammate is there
Protect the puck with your body and skate toward the safer boards to buy time to look up
Turn back into the slot to keep possession in the middle of the ice
Rim the puck hard around the boards before checking where your winger is
U13 / Peewee.explain: In the defensive high slot, a blind play through the middle is dangerous. If you have pressure and no scan, protect the puck first, move toward safer ice, and get your eyes up before choosing the next play.
U13 / Peewee.tip: Protect first, then scan and move the puck.

U13 / Peewee.sit: A good habit for a center on a faceoff win in the offensive zone is to immediately look back at their own defenseman to make sure the puck was caught cleanly.
U13 / Peewee.tip: After the win, scan opponents and get to your job.
U13 / Peewee.why: Once the puck is won back, the center should quickly find their check, tie up pressure when needed, and get to the net-front or slot area for a screen, tip, or loose puck instead of watching the defenseman.

U15 / Bantam.sit: You are the white team's right winger in the offensive zone. The black team's left defender blocks a shot and moves to the puck in the corner. The black center is already sprinting toward the boards on your side of the ice. Your own white center has pinched in at the far circle. What should you do right now?
opts: Crash the net in case the defender loses the puck
Move toward the black center to take away the boards
Back off to your own blue line to defend
Set up at the front of the net to screen
U15 / Bantam.explain: The black center racing to the boards signals the outlet is forming, and with your white center pinched deep, pressing them now is the only way to stop a clean breakout before the puck even moves. Crashing the net or screening only works when your team controls the puck, and drifting back first gives the black team a free pass out of their zone before your defense can set.

U18 / Midget.sit: You are a defenseman pinching at the left point in the offensive zone. Your center has the puck at the half-wall but is being angled hard into the corner. The opposing right winger is hovering near your blue line, and the opposing center has begun drifting toward the neutral zone. The puck has not moved yet. opts: Pinch deeper into the corner and help your center hold the puck there
